claims.original_statement: A uniformly cohomologically bounded inverse system is essentially constant if its cohomology systems are; the corresponding bounded cohomological criterion detects pro-isomorphisms.
claims.proved_statement: For objects with cohomology supported in the same r original degrees, any composite of r cohomologically zero maps is zero. This gives an explicit r-stage pro-zero construction; cones for input range [a,b] need at most b-a+2 such stages.
claims.hypotheses: A finite common set of original cohomological degrees in D(A); the actual truncation maps and actual inverse-system transitions.
claims.limits: The infinite-range counterexample has eventually zero cohomology in every degree and no zero transition. No unrestricted conservativity claim is made.
